extracted.intended_audience: readers/students of classical geometry and conic-section theory (Latin-reading mathematicians or historians of mathematics)
extracted.subtask_description: A Latin exposition on classical geometry: generation of solids by revolution, classification of cones, conic sections (circle, ellipse, parabola, hyperbola), privileged properties of parabola and spiral, sphere/cylinder relations, polygonal proportion methods, and warnings about paralogisms. Intended as an instructional/theoretical geometry text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generation of solids by revolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Cum semicirculo fixa diametro circúducitur donec ad corporum locum summ redeat, fit corpus quod sphaera vocatur. ... Sed si rectangulum eodem modo circundatur, fit cylindrus; si triangulum rectum eodem modo circumdu(t)ur, fit conus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines how rotating plane figures about an axis produces 3D solids: a semicircle about its diameter yields a sphere; a rectangle rotated about an axis yields a cylinder; a right triangle rotated yields a cone. Use these constructions as definitions for the corresponding solids and as bases for comparing their measures (areas, volumes, proportions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of cones (right, acute, obtuse)
rubrics_metrics.description: Huius tres sunt species, iuxta laterum rectum angulum continentium totidem differentias. Nam si latera sint qualia fit reus rectangulus conus. Si maius quod ztem est latus acutius rectus conus; quod si minus fit reus obtusus conus...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classifies cones by the relation of the generating triangle's sides/angles: a cone is 'rectus' (right) when the generating triangle has a right angle at the base, 'acutus' (acute) or 'obtusus' (obtuse) according to whether the corresponding generating side is respectively greater or lesser. Use these distinctions when reasoning about sections and proportional relations depending on cone type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conic sections: circle, ellipse, parabola, hyperbola (classification by plane)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ex his paret igitur, quod omnes hae figurae conveniunt in hoc, quod generantur ex sectione coni aut conorum bisariam: per planum ad perpendiculum erectum superficiei trianguli ... fieri potest circulus, ellipsis, parabola & hyperbola; nec posse ex uno cono plura genera inventiri, nisi secundum positiones (quinta figura...).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies that the principal plane sections of a cone produce circle, ellipse, parabola, or hyperbola depending on the position of the cutting plane relative to the cone's axis and sides: a plane perpendicular to the base yields a circle; an inclined plane that cuts the cone (but not through the axis extremes) yields an ellipse; a plane passing through a generating line yields a parabola; a plane intersecting both nappes (or producing opposite intersections) yields one or two hyperbolas. Use the plane-versus-axis/sides relation to identify the conic type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common geometric property of conic-section families
rubrics_metrics.description: Ex his parat ... quod omnes hae figurae generantur ex sectione coni aut conorum bisariam ... et quod quaecumque dicuntur communia coni, dum modo rectus fit vel fit rectan(g)ulus, vel acutus, vel obtusus, non ponuntur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States that the conic figures share genesis in cone sections; many shared propositions derive from this common origin. When proving properties that hold across conics, reduce to the cone-section construction and the plane's relation to the cone (axis, generating lines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Parabola — enumerated 'privilegia' (privileged properties)
rubrics_metrics.description: Paraboles autem privilegia sex propria sunt; Prima: ratio axis partium in ea est ut deductarum ex ipsis punctis perpendiculares ad paraboles circumferentiam duplicata. Secundum: cum fuerit ipsa perpendicularis equalis axis parti ... vocabitur ipsa perpendicularis latus rectum paraboles ... haec linea perpendiculares ordinatae. Tertium... (followed by further proportional and area relations and statements about equal portions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarises six characteristic properties attributed to the parabola: relationships of axis segments to ordinates (perpendiculars), definition and role of the latus rectum (when a perpendicular equals an axis-part), continuous proportionality among ordinates, equalities of portions with equal diameters, proportional relations between surface pieces and rectangles formed from base and axis parts, and further properties when three tangents/contingents coincide. Use these stated properties when deriving measurements or comparing parabola segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spiral — enumerated 'privilegia' (privileged properties)
rubrics_metrics.description: Spiralis autem lineae privilegia sex etiam sunt. Primum quidem: duca contingens ex fine illius accurrit perpendicularly ex initio ... semper tantum abscindens ex contingenti ut proportionem habeat ad circuli sub eodem ordine peripheria secundum ordinem ... Secundum: ex quocunque puncto prime spiralis educta contingens, occurrit perpendiculari ex initio eiusdem dimetiens ducta, tantam ex illa abscindens partem, quanta est portio circunferentiae circuli cuius semidiameter est linea ex initio lineae spiralis via ad punctum contingentis ... tertium: spatia spiraltum ita se habent: primum unitatis, secundum senarii, tertium duodenarii ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists key geometric relations of a (Archimedean-type) spiral: relations between tangent/perpendicular segments and corresponding circle arcs/sectors and scaling relations of successive spiral turns (multiplicative proportions like 1, 6, 12, ... are asserted). When using spiral constructions, relate linear segments (from origin to tangent/contact) to circular arcs and use the stated proportional scaling for successive turns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spherical and cylindrical proportional relations (privileges)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sphaerae proprietates ... proportio sphaerae superficiarum partium plano separatarum est velut partium diameter eodem plano diversarum, cum dimetiens tamen sphaera super planum perpendicularis fuerit. ... Inde cylindri privilegia duo. Cylindrus conotriplus est, cum altitudinem eandem ac basim habenti. Sphaera verò, cuius diameter fit equalis altitudini suae, & maior circulus basi cylindri ipse cylindrus sesquialter erit. ... funt sexaginta proprietates ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States proportional relations of spherical surface and volume parts cut by planes and diameters: surface/solid parts compare as rectangles or as squares of axis parts; cylinders have two primary 'privileges' (relations when altitudes and bases correspond). Use these proportion rules when comparing parts of spheres and cylinders and when transforming between cone and sphere measures (e.g., relating cone altitude to sphere semidiameter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Polygonal/reflex proportion method (constructional proportions for regular polygons)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reflexa proportio: ... quoad tres quantitatum, quarum proportio aggregati primae & secundae ad tertiam fuerit velucterti ad secundam; dicetur proportio reflexa. Example and method follow: 'dicetur reflexa bis propertio vocabitur' ... (method used in the construction of the heptagon inscribed in a circle — long explanation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the reflex proportion concept (a composed proportion among three magnitudes) and applies it to polygonal side relations (notably the heptagon inscribed in a circle). Use the compositional (resolutive) method described to reduce polygon side/arc problems to known numeric/proportional relations; follow the stepwise aggregation of ratios as exemplified for the heptagon construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paralogisms: definition, causes, and warning
rubrics_metrics.description: Paralogismi fiunt vel cum assumitur aliquid in constructione problematis quo non vtimur in demonstratione, vel cum vtimur principio non vero, sed verisimili, vel cum assumimus non demonstrata pro demonstratis. Indicio autem paralogismi est falsiexperimentum in conclusione vel mediis; aut deprehensio alicuius defectus ex his dictis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives a cautionary list of common fallacies in geometric reasoning: (1) assuming auxiliary facts in the problem that are not used in the proof, (2) using plausible but untrue principles, (3) treating undemonstrated statements as demonstrated. Detect paralogisms by checking for invalid experiments or defects in means/conclusion. As a methodological rubric: avoid undeclared or unproved assumptions; ensure every premise used is demonstrated or legitimately admissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolutive (composita) method guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Hanc cum reflexis implicibus confert, divisam demonstrare oportet. Atque hic est finis resolutoria methodi. Ab hoc igitur fine; composita methodus, quam preposuimus in laterum heptagoni demonstratione; initium sumit. Sed & in his quandoque error contingit, si quis non diligenter omnino adver-... (discussion of method and pitfalls).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes the compositional/resolutive method: begin from the desired conclusion (the end) and work back to known quantities, assembling component proportions to reach the target construction (used here for the heptagon). Warning: this method can produce errors if intermediate assumptions are not carefully checked; ensure that the 'medium' used is legitimate and not assumed to be itself the medium without justification.
